history.dynasty: Gorkha (Amar Singh Thapa), early 18th century; 19th/20th-century restorations
history.period: Early 18th century (CONFLICT: one source claims a 20th-century renovation by the ruler of Jaipur - verify)
history.summary: One of the Char Dham (Chota Char Dham) and the seat of Goddess Ganga, at ~3,100 m on the left bank of the Bhagirathi - CONFLICT: reported altitude varies 3,000-3,200 m; one source says 3,415 m (verify). Legend: King Bhagiratha's penance brought Ganga to earth; Shiva received her in his matted locks and released her as streams, one becoming the Bhagirathi. Near the temple stand Bhagirath Shila (the rock where Bhagiratha worshipped Shiva) and the submerged Jalmagna Shivling, visible only in winter. The white-granite ~20-ft temple was built in the early 18th century by Gorkha commander Amar Singh Thapa (Wikipedia: original structure by Thapa, restored in the 19th century). The Pandavas are said to have performed Deva Yajna here. Opens on Akshaya Tritiya (April/May), closes on Diwali (Oct/Nov); in winter the idol is worshipped at Mukhba (Mukhimath) village ~12 km downstream by the Semwal family of hereditary pujaris. Identity confirmed: the famous Char Dham Gangotri temple.

name: Gangotri Temple
town_description: Gangotri is a small Char Dham pilgrimage town in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand, on the banks of the Bhagirathi at ~3,100 m, about 100 km beyond Uttarkashi via Harsil. It is the last roadhead toward the Gaumukh glacier (18 km), source of the Bhagirathi, and the gateway to treks like Nandanvan, Tapovan and Kedartal.

travel.railway: Haridwar (~249 km per indiatraveltimes; some sources cite Rishikesh) - verify
travel.road: Well connected by road: Haridwar-Rishikesh-Uttarkashi-Harsil-Gangotri route; bus services from Uttarkashi, Rishikesh and Haridwar

visitor_information.best_time: May-June and September-October; avoid July-August monsoon (heavy rain, landslide risk)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily darshan roughly 6:15 AM-2:00 PM and 3:00-9:30 PM in the open season (per yatrachardham.in; verify). Temple open only from Akshaya Tritiya to Diwali; winter worship at Mukhba village.
